The audit trail is not erased: it keeps ids only. Requires the current password. Afterwards every token of the account stops working and the e-mail is free to register again. Cannot be undone. post.description: The host psychologist or a dependent registered in the meeting, while it is scheduled, from 10 minutes before it starts until it ends. Answers the server address, a token for this meeting's room only, this person's identity and the host's identity. The token is valid for 2 minutes: LiveKit checks it only on the first connection, and removing someone from the room does not invalidate the token they hold, so ask for a new token on every entry (also after a lost connection or a reload) and never store it. The token carries the dependent's nickname (the host's name for the psychologist), an opaque identity that is different in every meeting, and the role; nothing else. A dependent comes in without microphone or camera until the host allows them to speak, and cannot change their own name or metadata in the room: the raised hand is a data message to the host_identity, who keeps its state

Every call writes one MEETING_PARTICIPANTS_VIEWED entry per dependent listed, which each of them sees in GET /me/access-log. Everyone else only gets registered_count in the meeting

post.description: Dependents only. The meeting must be scheduled and not started. Idempotent: registering again changes nothing and answers 200 with the same meeting, even when it is full. The triage is not required. The capacity holds even when requests for the last seat arrive at the same time. Two consents are required first: the health data consent (POST /me/consents/health) and the participation term of the meeting, whose version in force goes in the body (accepted_participation_version) and is recorded together with the seat, with the time and the client IP. Without either, 400 CONSENT_REQUIRED and nothing is recorded
